scenes.headline: How a deep, narrow model reads a million tokens
scenes.sub: Step 5 Preview: 92 layers, sliding windows and Sparse GQA.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fathom! This model is ninety-two layers deep and reads a million tokens. Here is how it avoids reading them all.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Keep attention exact, but let each KV group pick 512 blocks of 8 tokens from a compressed index.
scenes.say: Keep attention exact, but let each group of heads pick five hundred and twelve blocks of eight tokens from a small index.

scenes.title: Three windows, then one full layer

steps.say: A token climbs twenty-three groups of four layers, on a narrow residual stream.

steps.note: a fixed cost at any length
steps.say: Three of every four layers look back only five hundred and twelve tokens.

steps.note: the only layers that see everything
steps.say: The fourth sees the whole context. That is where the sparse trick lives.

scenes.title: How a Sparse GQA layer chooses

steps.say: Every eight tokens, small index keys are pooled into one summary.
Each of the four key value groups scores every summary with its own query heads.
Each group keeps its own top five hundred and twelve blocks.
Then exact attention runs over those blocks, plus the query's own block.

steps.label: full attention
steps.say: Full attention reads every earlier token.

steps.label: sliding window
steps.say: A sliding layer reads only a recent window.

steps.label: chosen blocks
steps.say: A sparse layer reads a fixed budget of chosen blocks, wherever they are.
In the blog's drawing, the indexer pools keys into block keys, and each group scores them.
Each group then reads only its selected blocks and the current one.

scenes.title: Cache held at 1M tokens
scenes.note: the sliding windows save the memory, not the sparsity
scenes.say: The cache still holds every token. It shrinks about four times, thanks to the sliding windows.

scenes.label: of attention-side FLOPs per new token go to the indexer at 1M
scenes.say: Sparsity saves reading. But at a million tokens, the indexer is most of the attention arithmetic.

scenes.text: Sparse GQA trades memory for reads: every token stays cached, but a query reads only what its group chose.
scenes.mark: a query reads only what its group chose
scenes.say: Every token stays cached. A query reads only what its group chose.

recap: Blocks of 8 tokens, chosen per group
The indexer is the new cost
scenes.say: Three windows to one full layer. Blocks of eight, chosen per group. And the indexer is the new cost.
